output.method_plain: We started with eight nearby sales from public records, all within about 4 miles and sold between August 2025 and June 2026. Each sale price was adjusted to match your house for date of sale (0.33% a month), living area ($75 a sq ft), finished basement ($25 a sq ft), lot size ($5,000 an acre, first 3 acres of difference only), age, bedrooms and baths, central air and garage. Sales that were not raised ranches also had 8% taken off for style. The range runs from the lowest to the highest adjusted price among the five sales not flagged as weak, rounded to $5,000: $615,000 to $730,000. The indicated value is $660,000 and the median adjusted price is $645,000. This is a comparative market analysis, not an appraisal.

weak_comps.why: 10 Stonewall Dr is a larger Colonial that sold about 15 months ago, so its price needed large adjustments (26% gross) for size, style and time.
195 S White Rock Rd is a much larger Contemporary on a bigger lot, 1.5 miles away and sold almost 14 months ago, so adjustments were heavy (31% gross).
226 White Pond Rd is a raised ranch like yours but it is 3.81 miles away, the farthest of the eight.
16 Mountain View Dr is a raised ranch but about 550 sq ft smaller and sold nearly 13 months ago, so it needed a large upward adjustment (+$89,800) and it sets the low end of the range.

output.reasoning: I suggest listing at $675,000, a little above the $660,000 indicated value and in the upper-middle part of the $615,000 to $730,000 range. The adjustments leave out several things that could help you: your 4.18-acre lot is bigger than nearly all the comparables (the lot adjustment stops at 3 acres), the kitchen was updated in 2019 and the windows in 2016, and town-wide values appear to have risen about 8% between 2025 and 2026, more than our time adjustment allows. The possible pond at the lot's edge is also not counted, because only about 13% of it falls inside your lot lines. Pulling the other way are frontage on a state route, oil heat, no garage and original baths, none of which are priced in. A higher price leaves room to negotiate but risks a longer wait if buyers see the house as above the recent sales. A price near $660,000 would likely draw offers sooner.
things_that_would_change_it: A survey showing the pond is on your lot and can be used by the owner would support a higher price.
A home inspection finding problems with the roof (installed 2012), septic, well or oil heating system would lower the price.
Traffic noise or road exposure from Route 292 that buyers find significant at showings would push the price down.
A newer sale or competing listing nearby at higher prices than these comparables would support the upper end of the range.

and do not invent sales, prices or facts: use only the data you are given.

Write for a homeowner, in plain words, no jargon. This is a comparative market analysis, not an appraisal; never
call it an appraisal or a valuation of record.

- method_plain: which sales were used and why they are comparable, what was adjusted (date of sale, size, finished
  basement, lot, age, rooms, central air, garage) and how the range was formed. 3 to 5 sentences.
- weak_comps: the comparables that are weaker guides (large adjustments, distance, a different style), with one
  sentence each. Use their rank numbers.
- recommended_price: your recommended list price, a round figure, normally inside the computed range. If you go
  outside it, say why in the reasoning.
- reasoning: why this price: where it sits in the range, what the adjustments leave out (listed in
  not_adjusted_for), and the trade-off between a higher price and time on market. 3 to 6 sentences.
- things_that_would_change_it: 2 to 4 facts that would move the price if confirmed.

Never mention schools' quality, neighbourhood make-up, safety or crime, or the kind of buyer the house suits.
Do not mention the seller's personal circumstances (you are not given them).
